setlist.title: Beat It On Down The Line

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Spanish Jam** (2 reviews): The sixteen-minute Spanish Jam features extraordinary flamenco interplay; The Spanish jam is described as a flamenco masterpiece [5][12]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): The first China Cat sounds lower in key than later versions, with fast playing [10]
- **The Eleven** (1 review): A rare China Cat to Eleven transition works well in this performance [10]
- **The Other One** (1 review): The Other One features early draft lyrics in this performance [14]

## The recordings

- **gd1968-01-17.sbd.cotsman.11795.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 15 songs; 96 min; rated 4.12/5 by 24 [1]. Said about its sound: Sound is good but could be better, with a few lost bits; The recording is crystal clear for its time, with 68 classics in glory; The performance is raw and a little gritty, described as the height of Pigpen [4][7][9][13]
- **gd1968-01-17.sbd.jeff.3927.shnf**: soundboard; 14 songs; 85 min; rated 5/5 by 4 [2]. Said about its sound: Very noticeable hiss and hum suggest an extra cassette generation in the lineage; Channel weirdness at the beginning of CD1 track 3, with the start missing [2]
- **gd1968-01-17.sbd.jeff.fixed-3927.7995.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 14 songs; 85 min; rated 3.8/5 by 10 [3]. Said about its sound: The file is hissy and muddy, sourced from a later generation; Very noticeable hiss and hum, with channel weirdness at the start of CD1 track 3 [3][12]

## Around the show

- The band introduces several new songs after returning from an out-of-town tour [8]
- Phil's book calls these shows the most visionary music they had played to date [11]
- Sound quality is inferior to the Tour of the Great Northwest shows [5]
- The show falls short of later magical shows in tightness and sound quality [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1968-01-17.sbd.cotsman.11795.shnf**: transferred by Jeff Cotsman, Matt Vernon and Raoul Duke; source: SBD>MR>C>D>CD>EAC>SHN [1]. Also: First known renditions as of July 2002, possibly with a second cassette generation; First few notes of Dark Star and New Potato Caboose are clipped; Edits and encoding for the Music Never Stopped Project by Matt Vernon and J. Cotsman [1]
- **gd1968-01-17.sbd.jeff.3927.shnf**: source: MSR>cass>dat>cdrs [2]. Also: Lineage listed as MSR to cassette, DAT, CDRs, then EAC, WAV, CoolEdit, WAV, SHN [2]
- **gd1968-01-17.sbd.jeff.fixed-3927.7995.sbeok.shnf**: source: MSR> cass> dat> cdrs [3]. Also: Same lineage as SHNID 3927 through d1t09, with later tracks having an unexplained fix [3]
